conflicts: Fax 888-556-2128 is printed on Humana's member 'Appeal or Grievance Form' (Y0040_GHHJX8LENa_C: 'may be sent to us by mail or fax ... Fax Number: 888-556-2128') and in some 2026 member Evidences of Coverage, but Humana's provider guide 642103ALL0125 labels 888-556-2128 'Commercial standard fax'. Humana's provider documents for Medicare Advantage list no standard appeal fax. Do not use it for provider claim disputes or appeals.

Fax 800-949-2961 is Humana's 'Medicare expedited fax' (guide 642103ALL0125). Expedited appeals are for services not yet given; they never apply to payment for care already given. Do not use it for claim appeals.

Participating providers have no Medicare appeal rights of their own at Humana: the 2026 directory says 'Participating providers do not have grievance and appeal rights on behalf of themselves'. Their route is the dispute process above, then the Provider Concierge escalation, then the arbitration terms of the agreement.

Dispute filing clock: the 2026 manual counts 18 months from 'the date the provider received notice of the original claim determination'; the 2025 manual (FINAL589003ALL1024) said 'within 18 months of the date the claim was paid'. Use the 2026 wording.
payers.no_fax_reason: Humana publishes no fax for provider claim payment disputes, reconsiderations or appeals on Medicare Advantage claims. Its live claim-payment page, its 2026 provider manual, its claim-payment inquiry guide (642103ALL0125) and its August 2026 tip sheet name only Availity, phone and mail (Humana Correspondence, P.O. Box 14601). Humana's faxes are for records it asked for (866-305-6655) and record-review disputes (888-815-8912) only.

conflicts: Humana's 2026 Indiana D-SNP provider resource guide is a placeholder PDF ('Coming Soon'), so no D-SNP-specific provider appeal page exists yet; the routes above come from Humana's Indiana Medicaid pages and its national guide.
Humana's guide lists 'Medicaid/duals expedited fax 855-336-6220' for expedited requests only (pre-service); it is not for claims.

Indiana FIDE status: the state's waiver says 'MCEs are required to maintain a fully integrated dual eligible special needs plan (FIDE D-SNP)' and 'Effective January 1, 2026, the State will require exclusively aligned enrollment'; Humana's own page calls the plan 'Humana PathWays Dual Care (HMO-POS D-SNP)'.
payers.no_fax_reason: Humana Healthy Horizons in Indiana publishes no fax for provider claim disputes or appeals: informal disputes go by Availity, mail or email, formal disputes by mail or email, and dual/Medicaid appeals by Availity or mail. The only dual fax in Humana's guide (855-336-6220) is for expedited (pre-service) requests.
payers.notes: Indiana's PathWays waiver (Indiana PathWays for Aging 1915(b) waiver IN.017.00.03, 2026-01-27, https://secure.in.gov/fssa/files/PathWaysBJan2026.PDF) says 'Effective January 1, 2026, the State will require exclusively aligned enrollment for full-benefit dual eligible PathWays enrollees who choose to enroll in the FIDE-SNP.' A non-contracted provider who signs a waiver of payment from the member is a party to an integrated reconsideration: 42 CFR 422.629 (eCFR) (https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-42/chapter-IV/subchapter-B/part-422/subpart-M/section-422.629, read 2026-11-23) lists 'An assignee of the enrollee (that is, a physician or other provider who has furnished or intends to furnish a service to the enrollee and formally agrees to waive any right to payment from the enrollee for that service).'
